title: Outreach Voice Template
summary: Patrik's original voice template, the source of truth for all cold outreach.
content:
Outreach Voice Template

Written by Patrik. 2026-03-09. This is the source of truth for all cold outreach.

The Email (Base Template)

Subject: really impressed by [Company Name] work

{First name}, I came across your stuff the other day and honestly your work looks solid. I can tell you guys care about your work.

Not assuming anything, just thought it would be cool to see about possibly working together. I work for a few construction companies in Phoenix on showcasing their hard work to the public on their websites and social medias.

If you ever want to talk shop, I'm around.

{DEFAULT GMAIL SIGNATURE}

Patrik's Rewrite Example (THE STANDARD)

This is what a personalized email looks like. Study this:

Bryan,

What the Y is doing across Phoenix looks really solid. I can tell you guys care about your work.

I remember going to the Y as a kid after school it was always a great place for me.

Not assuming anything, just thought it would be cool to see about possibly working together. I work for a few construction companies in Phoenix on showcasing their hard work to the public on their websites and social medias.

Recently, I've even been designing AI systems for businesses, which has been pretty interesting although I don't know if that would work for the Y as an organization. It could help you as a person possibly.

If you ever want to talk shop, I'm around.

What makes this better than the template:

  • Opens by referencing what the Y specifically does across Phoenix (not generic "your stuff")
  • Adds a personal memory ("I remember going to the Y as a kid"). This is the kind of detail that makes an email feel real.
  • AI paragraph is casual, almost uncertain ("I don't know if that would work for the Y"). Not a pitch.
  • The whole thing reads like one human talking to another, not a template with the name swapped.

Voice Rules

  • EVERY email MUST open with the prospect's first name. "{First name}," is not optional. If you don't have their first name, find it on their website, LinkedIn, or Google before sending. Never send an email without addressing them by name.
  • This is a real person reaching out because he noticed something. Not a pitch.
  • No case studies. No stats. No "we just wrapped a project for..." Instant spam vibes.
  • No clever hooks or subject line tricks.
  • Subject lines need the same thought as the email body. "really impressed by [Company Name] work" is the base, but if the company name is long (3+ words), shorten it or rephrase so it reads natural. Examples: "really impressed by your work" / "your guys' work is solid" / "really impressed by what [short name] is doing" / "had to reach out". The subject should match the casual tone of the email. If it reads stiff with the full business name crammed in, rewrite it.
  • No assumptions about what they need or what's wrong with their current presence.
  • "I can tell you guys care about your work" = the energy. Genuine respect, not flattery.
  • Keep it short. If it feels like a brochure, delete it and start over.
  • Default Gmail signature on every email. No custom sign-offs.
  • The email opens the door. The relationship closes the deal. Email 1 is not trying to sell anything.
  • DO NOT repeat the same words/phrases across emails. "Solid" should appear in maybe 1-2 emails out of 15, not all of them. Find different ways to say what you mean each time.
  • Every email must feel like it was written for that one person. If you can swap the name and company and the email still works unchanged, it's too generic. Rewrite it.
  • Adapt the pitch line to the industry. Match the client description to the prospect's world. Examples: "construction companies", "tech companies", "nonprofits here in Phoenix", "a couple different clients in Phoenix", "companies in the trades". Don't tell the YMCA you do construction. There's a lot of ways to say it -- vary it.

AI Systems Mention

Patrik wants to occasionally mention designing AI systems for businesses. Rules:

  • Do NOT include this in every email. Maybe 1 out of 5 emails, tops.
  • Only when it could genuinely apply to the person or their business.
  • Frame it casually: "Recently, I've even been designing AI systems for businesses, which has been pretty interesting although I don't know if that would work for [company]. It could help you as a person possibly."
  • Never hard-pitch AI. It's a soft mention, almost an afterthought.
  • If it doesn't fit, leave it out entirely. Most emails should NOT have this.

Personalization

Jacob MUST customize per prospect. This is not optional:

  • Research their actual business. Reference specific projects, locations, specialties.
  • Add a personal touch when possible (a memory, an observation, something real).
  • Vary the opening. Don't start every email the same way. "I came across your stuff the other day" should not appear in more than 2-3 emails per batch.
  • Vary the compliment. "Looks solid" in one, "looks really well done" in another, "can tell you guys put in the work" in another. Never repeat the same phrase across the batch.
  • If you can't find something specific, dig harder. Google them. Check their Instagram. Look at their projects page. The template-as-is is a last resort, not the default.

Multi-Touch (Volume Strategy)

One email isn't the strategy. Showing up repeatedly is.

  • Email 1: This template
  • Email 2 (5 days): Different angle, still casual. Reference something they posted or built.
  • Email 3 (7 days): Even shorter. "Still thinking about what you guys are building. Let me know if you ever want to grab coffee."
  • Touches 4+: Mix of LinkedIn, Instagram follow, maybe a DM. Just being present.

Never get weird about it. Never escalate the pressure. Same guy, same energy, every time.

What This Replaces

The 36 revised drafts in jacob-revised-drafts.md are DEAD. Do not send them. They sound like a brochure. The structural fixes from the 3 Piece Special are irrelevant for this voice. Start fresh from this template for every new batch.
